note: Papers and reports read in the lab, newest first. Each entry: what it found in one line, and what it changed here in one line. Evidence tier is how far it was read: full, abstract, or report. Internal identifiers never appear here.

entries.title: Music as Code (theme page and essays, 2026)
entries.found: Reitz, the author of Requests, returns to music through code: PyTheory (theory as data structures), a mini DAW in the Python REPL, NumPy as the synth engine, and Interpretations, an album of twenty-four scripts that render to WAV. Premise: code and music are both languages for structuring time.
entries.here: A 2026 row on the History page next to the lab's own: the score is the script, arrived at from the other direction.

entries.title: The History of Live Coding: From Bell Labs to the Algorave
entries.found: Computer music starts with the Illiac Suite (1957) and Max Mathews' MUSIC I at Bell Labs; live coding gets its name and its one rule at TOPLAP's founding in Hamburg in February 2004 (show us your screens); Tidal Cycles (2009), the first algorave (2012), Sonic Pi (2013), ICLC (2015), Strudel (2022), TOPLAP at twenty (2024).
entries.here: The lab's History page and a post: Code as Music is a Sonic Pi program driven by the lab's own state, the TOPLAP rule applied to infrastructure.

entries.title: ZTA: Zero Token Architecture (Kelsey Hightower, PlatformCon 2026)
entries.found: Infer once, export the result, run it without inference. An agent that rebuilds the same table by inference every run is a cache miss on purpose; caching is the oldest idea in computing. Teams that lost unlimited tokens revolted because they had become codependent, and most infrastructure was never designed, it accreted.
entries.here: Test planned: a ZTA audit of every recurring task here, in three buckets (inference every run, exported script, must stay inferred and why), with the top three converted (deploy verification first) and each export recording what it assumed and when it re-derives. Absolute counts before and after.

entries.title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
entries.found: A finished discovery run is a tree of attempts with recorded outcomes; replayed as a simulator, thousands of alternative exploration policies can be scored at zero execution cost before one is redeployed. Only the exploration-policy code changes. Reported up to 162x fewer agent calls than SimpleTES; the baselines are the authors' own.
entries.here: History as a simulator is the same rule as the talk above, applied to search. Test planned: before any re-run of a failed recurring task, the runner reads the last five outcomes and names a checkable change (a commit, a config diff, a version bump), or refuses.

entries.title: DeepSeek-Prover-V2: Advancing Formal Mathematical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Subgoal Decomposition
entries.found: A large general model decomposes a theorem into Lean 4 subgoals with sorry placeholders; a 7B prover solves each; the composed proofs seed reinforcement learning. 88.9% on MiniF2F-test at Pass@8192 and 47 of 658 PutnamBench problems.
entries.here: Big model plans once, small model runs the loop: the shape of the lab's model lanes. The headline number is 8,192 attempts per problem; read the denominator.

entries.title: AI Will Become Mathematicians' Co-Pilot (Terence Tao interview)
entries.found: Lean and mathlib let twenty strangers collaborate on one proof without trusting each other, because the compiler checks every contribution. Formalization costs ten times the conventional route today; AI could bring it under one. AI has shown no ability to split a problem into easier pieces, and the precious training data is the failed attempts nobody publishes.
entries.here: The receipt ledger is the lab's Lean: trust the check, not the collaborator. Red rows in the test pipeline are the published failures.

entries.title: Interpreting and Improving Large Language Models in Arithmetic Calculation
entries.found: Fewer than 5% of attention heads carry two-operand arithmetic in LLaMA2; knocking them out costs about 70% of accuracy. Fine-tuning 32 of 1,024 heads matches or beats full fine-tuning on maths without the usual regression on other tasks.
entries.here: Targeted change over blanket change. If the local Qwen lane ever needs a tune, a narrow one is the honest option.

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence in Biological Sciences
entries.found: Narrative review of AI in medicine, agriculture and industrial biotech, pre-LLM and without data of its own. The useful part is the challenges section: a chest X-ray classifier learned to detect chest tubes rather than pneumothorax, and few models reach clinical practice because data access, reproducibility and accountability block them.
entries.here: Shortcut learning is a probe that passes on a proxy signal. Folded into the planned FDIA probe test as a case.

entries.title: Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents (Paper2Agent)
entries.found: A paper becomes an MCP server plus an agent; each extracted tool is validated against the paper's own reported outputs and locked. 74 of 100 computational biology papers agentified, 593 of 599 tools validated, 91.2% on tutorial questions against 80.3% for raw repository access.
entries.here: Test planned: agentify the lab's own Infrastructure as Music repository from its README; numeric tools within 3%, audio and SVG hash-equal, no manual fixes.

entries.title: AI in Science: Early Insights
entries.venue: Google, Google DeepMind, MIT FutureTech (working paper, September 2026)
entries.found: 637 panel-recruited scientists, 15 million Gemini interactions, 2,600 specialized models. 47% use AI daily; LLMs and specialized models are complements; the bottleneck moved downstream for 44% and 41% report a growing backlog of untested hypotheses. The time saving, just under 7 hours a week, is self-reported.
entries.here: The test pipeline on this site is a backlog by construction; the number that matters is how fast rows move from planned to a result.

entries.title: Why AI is speeding up scientific research but not lab experiments
entries.found: 89% of those who save time with AI spend more than a tenth of it checking outputs, 46% more than a quarter; AI progresses where there is ground truth.
entries.here: Verification is the tax on speed. A test without a checkable pass condition is a wish; the verification tax on this lab's own completion claims is now measured.

entries.title: Google DeepMind publications, March to September 2026 (21 entries)
entries.found: Seven of 21 are alignment and safety evaluation: scheming honeypots, sabotage auditing across 17 agentic scenarios, proactive failure discovery, red-teaming at scale. Three study agents in social and economic settings; five are essays on consciousness and AGI.
entries.here: Evaluate propensity, not only capability. A fabricated-receipt honeypot for delegated tasks joined the test pipeline.

entries.title: Mapping trust in artificial intelligence across Europe: a cluster-based comparative analysis
entries.found: 35 countries, K-means: Digital Champions, Sceptical Pragmatists (high infrastructure, low trust) and Cautious Emergents. Usage and trust move independently.
entries.here: Usage is not sufficient for trust; adoption copy names the job and the data boundary first.

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Restructuring of Saudi Labor Markets
entries.found: 120 sector-years, fixed effects with an instrument: routine-intensive employment down (β −0.41), demand for high-skill digital competencies up (β +0.67).
entries.here: Held as a value rather than filed as a finding: the skill that survives is the one that operates the system.

entries.title: Single-phase fault diagnosis in distribution networks via cyber-secure hybrid models of artificial intelligence
entries.found: An autoencoder, CNN and BiLSTM hybrid keeps accuracy and F1 under false data injection attacks where single-point benchmarks degrade.
entries.here: A health probe that trusts its inputs is only as good as the inputs. Test planned: a forged all-clear state file must be caught by an independent second signal.

entries.title: Teaching for artificial or human intelligence? A critical perspective on assessment during the AI era
entries.found: Argues for AI-proof assessment that protects the abilities to Discern, Engage, Evaluate and Produce. A position paper, no data.
entries.here: Closed-book practice, explanations written by the learner, not read from the sheet.

entries.title: Construction of self-supervised learning models for educational scenarios based on data-efficient artificial intelligence
entries.found: With 10% of labels, AUC 0.520 against 0.5225 fully supervised. The headline gain over the baseline is 3 to 6 percent at an absolute AUC near chance.
entries.here: Publish absolute and prospective numbers, never only the delta. Now a rule for every metric this lab publishes.

entries.title: Artificial intelligence-driven early warning for online learner dropout: temporal explainability and theory-grounded intervention
entries.found: 32,593 registrations, LightGBM with temporal SHAP: AUC 0.727 before the course opens, 0.911 by day 120; the engagement persistence ratio leads and a second-half collapse of activity is the signal. Prospective figure to plan against: 0.72 to 0.75.
entries.here: The signal lives in the relationship between measurements over time. Test planned: a trend watchdog over a 24 hour window.

entries.title: Creativity in the age of artificial intelligence: an exploratory study segmenting perceptions of human and machine-made art
entries.found: 19 works shown beside AI reproductions; visitors split into Traditionalists, Visualists, Skeptics and AI Enthusiasts. The co-creator framing is the curatorial problem.
entries.here: Every piece on the art page states how it was made; ownership, not framing, closes the question.

entries.title: AI/ML-driven polymerization in autonomous flow reactors
entries.found: An autonomous flow reactor closes the loop between model and experiment for polymerization; the bottleneck is the physical cycle, not the model.
entries.here: The same shape as the lab's own loops: the slow step is the experiment, so instrument it.

entries.title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
entries.found: The exploration policy of a discovery loop can improve itself against evolving simulated worlds; results on 8 tasks in 3 domains against a frozen-policy baseline.
entries.here: History as a simulator is the same rule as the talk above, applied to search. Test planned: before any re-run of a failed recurring task, the runner reads the last five outcomes and names a checkable change (a commit, a config diff, a version bump), or refuses.

entries.title: An Architecture for Long-Horizon Agents: Levels, Ticks and Cascaded Intelligence
entries.found: Judgment, labor and deterministic tiers; work moves up a tier only after review and escalation; a tick is the unit of accounting.
entries.here: A description of the harness this lab runs, written by someone else; the review-and-escalate cascade is held until a reviewed trigger exists.

entries.title: AgentPProf: Semantic Profiler for Long-Horizon AI Agents
entries.found: Profiling rather than tracing: trajectories become operation stacks and flame graphs, so cost concentrates where it is spent.
entries.here: First profile of the lab's own agent runs produced the same week; per-turn evidence already existed, the flame graph made it legible.

entries.title: OpenAgentFlow: a system-wide safety boundary for heterogeneous agent fleets
entries.found: A control-plane and action-plane split: every action, GUI, API, tool or planned, is normalized into one event stream that a policy layer can gate.
entries.here: Matches the lab's gate on irreversible-and-external actions; the event stream is the part still missing.

entries.title: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
entries.found: An evolvable harness decomposed into five modules evolved independently on benchmark-disjoint tasks; consistent gains on unseen tasks.
entries.here: Blueprint for the lab's own harness experiments: modular, benchmark-disjoint, so the loop does not overfit the eval at hand.

entries.title: Authorization Architectures for Tool-Using AI Agents
entries.found: Where the authorization decision sits, at the tool, the gateway or the planner, changes what a compromised component can reach.
entries.here: The lab's secrets sit behind an egress proxy the model never sees; the paper's map is the one used to explain why.

entries.title: Emergence World: Adversarial Stress-Testing of Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
entries.found: Adversarial environments that stress coordination over long horizons surface failures single-run benchmarks miss.
entries.here: Input to the replay-worlds plan.

entries.title: Red-Teaming Auto Mode: Improving Blocking Classifiers Against Malign Coding Agents
entries.found: Blocking classifiers for autonomous coding agents improve when red-teamed against the agent's own strategies rather than static prompts.
entries.here: Noted for the sandbox tier; no change yet.

entries.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
entries.found: 176 matched settings across four models on SWE-Bench Verified and Terminal-Bench: context management and tool design move outcomes more than the model choice does.
entries.here: Backs the lab's lane routing and context pruning; the persona prompt budget is enforced at build time.

entries.title: How Do Agent Harnesses Create Value?
entries.found: On τ²-bench with 265 matched cells, task-specific plans lift oracle-verified success by 7.2 points, mostly on the hard tail.
entries.here: Plans per task class, not per run.

entries.title: When AI Agents Commit: Cognitive Serializability
entries.found: An agent's mutation derives from reads, evidence, policy and delegated authority that can each go stale before the commit; valid at read time is not valid at commit time.
entries.here: The receipt verifier now expires standing grants after thirty minutes and refuses a claim whose reads are not logged.

entries.title: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness (SoL-Pi)
entries.found: Auto-discovered harness mechanisms, action execution and observation handling among them, found by a research loop rather than by hand.
entries.here: Read with ModularRSI; the lab's harness changes stay hand-reviewed for now.

entries.title: RAFT: Stateful RAG for Troubleshooting Agents
entries.found: Closed cases become directed timelines and retrieval happens at the entry to a case, not mid-stream.
entries.here: The lab's incident files are one RCA per file for the same reason.

entries.title: The Mechanics of a Swarm
entries.found: An external reconstruction of the agents-on-a-public-wiki episode of mid-2026: 14,591 revisions, coordination without a coordinator.
entries.here: Read with the counter-swarm paper; the lab's inbound agent stays memory-less and paired-sender only.

entries.title: Counter-Swarm Doctrine: Containing Coordinated Agent Intrusions
entries.found: Position paper: the unit of defense is the coordination channel, not the individual agent.
entries.here: Candidate improvements filed for consensus; none adopted yet.

entries.title: Can LLMs Act as Agent Swarm Orchestrators? (SwarmBench)
entries.found: A benchmark scoring orchestration on accuracy, efficiency and cost together; orchestrators that win on accuracy often lose on cost.
entries.here: Cost is a scored axis in the lab's model-lane routing.

entries.title: A Scalable Trust Discovery Architecture for the Internet of Agents
entries.found: Three layers, root, registry and record, so an agent's identity and permissions can be discovered without a central broker.
entries.here: Read for the day two agents outside this lab need to trust each other; not there yet.

entries.title: The effects of remote work on collaboration among information workers
entries.venue: Nature Human Behaviour (Yang et al.; preprint arXiv 2007.15584)
entries.found: Firm-wide remote work made collaboration networks more static and siloed, with less synchronous communication.
entries.here: Read while designing how the lab's agents and people share one room; the shared channel is deliberate.
